subject: human kidneys
title: Your Blood Goes Through a Filter Nearly 30 Times a Day

scenes.text: Every drop of your blood goes through a filter nearly thirty times a day.
The filters are your kidneys, each one about the size of your fist.
Together they process about a hundred and fifty quarts of blood every day.
Inside each kidney, about a million tiny filters pull out waste and extra water.
Only one or two quarts of it leave your body as urine. The rest goes back in.
Nearly thirty times a day. And you only need one kidney to live.

description:
According to the NIH's kidney institute (NIDDK), your two fist-sized kidneys filter about 150 quarts of blood a day and turn only 1 to 2 quarts into urine. With roughly 5 litres (about 5.3 quarts) of blood in an adult, that is close to 30 passes a day.
Each kidney holds about a million filtering units called nephrons, and people can live healthy lives with just one kidney.
What other organ do you think works this hard?
first_comment: Bonus: the kidneys get about a fifth of every heartbeat's blood. Which organ should we cover next?
